land.text: the eleven states that seceded between 20 December 1860 and 20 May 1861 (Cliopatria's 1861 shape, less western Virginia)

predecessors.note: Formed at Montgomery on 8 February 1861 by the first six seceded states (the researcher's reading of the page's secession list); Texas followed in February-March, Virginia, Arkansas, Tennessee and North Carolina in April-June.

land.text: the last Confederate shape of 1865, reoccupied by the Union armies between February and May 1865

successors.note: The CSA page: the states were readmitted to Congress after ratifying the Thirteenth Amendment (undated on the page); the 1867 military districts are not on the page.

rulers.name: Jefferson Davis
rulers.title: President
rulers.note: The page lists Davis as president 1861-1865 and Alexander H. Stephens as vice president; 'On February 22, 1862, Davis was inaugurated as president' (after the provisional term).

union.text: the portion of the New Mexico Territory south of the 34th parallel

correction.text: Cliopatria's 1861 shape without western Virginia (Union-held after the 1861 campaign), with the whole state of Texas (which seceded on 1 February 1861) and the Confederate Arizona Territory south of the 34th parallel proclaimed 1 August 1861

keyframe_review.note: 1.71 M km2. The CSA page's infobox gives no area, only the 1860 population (9,103,332). Computed with the gazetteer, the shape holds 98% of West Virginia, which the Western Virginia page says the Union army occupied 'for the rest of the war' after the May-December 1861 campaign (the shape is right only for the Confederate claim), only 55% of Texas (the Republic of Texas outline, though the whole state seceded on 1 February per the CSA page) and almost nothing of Confederate Arizona (proclaimed 1 August 1861, Confederate Arizona page). It also touches 5% of Kentucky and 2% of Missouri, handled as contested zones in the ledger.

union.text: the portion of the New Mexico Territory south of the 34th parallel

correction.text: Cliopatria's 1862 shape plus the whole of Texas and, until the Union occupation of 8 July 1862, Confederate Arizona

keyframe_review.note: 1.49 M km2 (87% of the 1861 area); the CSA page says that 'as of the end of April' 1862 the Confederacy 'still controlled territory holding 72% of its population'. The shape agrees with the dated Union gains on the Western Theater page (Forts Henry and Donelson February, New Orleans 28 April, Corinth 29 May 1862: it holds 57% of Tennessee, 87% of Louisiana, 95% of Mississippi) but is silent on Nashville and Memphis, North Carolina's coast and Norfolk (not on the pages: unverified, page budget). Same Texas and Arizona correction as 1861.

correction.text: Cliopatria's 1863 shape plus the whole of Texas

keyframe_review.note: 1.32 M km2. The shape has lost the Mississippi River line (Mississippi 60%, Louisiana 56%): the page dates Vicksburg 4 July and Port Hudson 8 July 1863 ('the entire Mississippi River was in Union hands'). Tennessee falls to 17% (Chickamauga 19-20 September, Chattanooga 24-25 November 1863 on the page; Knoxville not on it). Same Texas correction.

correction.text: Cliopatria's 1864 shape plus the whole of Texas

keyframe_review.note: 1.25 M km2; the CSA page: 'early 1864' the Confederacy controlled 53% of its population. Arkansas falls to 8% by this shape (the Trans-Mississippi page is silent on Little Rock and the Arkansas River: unverified, page budget); the Red River campaign of 1864 'was thwarted' on the same page, so north-west Louisiana stays Confederate. Georgia is still 95%: Atlanta fell on 1 September 1864 and Savannah on 22 December (Western Theater page), so the shape is the situation before the autumn campaigns. Same Texas correction.

correction.text: Cliopatria's 1865 shape plus the whole of Texas; the remaining land is surrendered between 9 April and 26 May 1865

keyframe_review.note: 1.08 M km2; the CSA page: 'early 1865' the Confederacy held 'only one-third of its population'. Georgia is 43% (Savannah 22 December 1864), South Carolina 97% (Columbia fell 17 February 1865), Virginia still 87% (Richmond fell 2-3 April, Lee surrendered 9 April, Johnston 26 April, the Trans-Mississippi Department 26 May 1865), so the shape is the January picture and the ledger carries the collapse. Same Texas correction.

region.text: South Carolina, Mississippi, Florida, Alabama, Georgia and Louisiana, which seceded 20 December 1860 to 26 January 1861 and formed the Confederacy at Montgomery

ledger.note: February 1861: the Confederate States of America is formed at Montgomery, Alabama. 'The Confederacy was formed on February 8, 1861.' (infobox 'Provisional constitution: February 8, 1861'). The page lists South Carolina (20 December 1860), Mississippi (9 January), Florida (10 January), Alabama (11 January), Georgia (19 January) and Louisiana (26 January) as having seceded first; which of them formed the first Confederacy is the researcher's reading.

region.text: the whole state of Texas, which seceded on 1 February 1861

ledger.note: February 1861: Texas joins. 'Texas (February 1; referendum February 23)'. The page gives no admission date; the USA dossier reads the Territory page as 2 March 1861.

region.text: Virginia in its 1861 limits, western counties included (the later West Virginia), which seceded on 17 April 1861

ledger.note: 17 April 1861: Virginia secedes. 'Virginia (April 17; referendum May 23, 1861)'. The page gives secession dates, not admission dates; western Virginia is lost again in July (see below).

region.text: Arkansas, which seceded on 6 May 1861

ledger.note: 6 May 1861: Arkansas secedes. 'Arkansas (May 6)'.

region.text: North Carolina, which seceded on 20 May 1861

ledger.note: 20 May 1861: North Carolina secedes. 'North Carolina (May 20)'.
29 May 1861: the capital moves from Montgomery to Richmond, Virginia. 'Montgomery, Alabama (until May 29, 1861)'; infobox 'Richmond, Virginia (until April 2-3, 1865)'.

region.text: Tennessee, which seceded on 7 May and voted on 8 June 1861

ledger.note: June 1861: Tennessee, the eleventh state, joins. 'Tennessee (May 7; referendum June 8)'. East Tennessee's Unionist counties are not on the page.

region.text: western Virginia, where the Union column attacked at Philippi on 3 June 1861

ledger.note: 3 June 1861: fighting for western Virginia begins at Philippi. 'On June 3, a Union column under the command of Brigadier General' drove off the Confederate camp; the campaign table gives 'May to December, 1861'.

region.text: western Virginia (the later West Virginia) outside the small southern part Cliopatria keeps

ledger.note: July 1861: western Virginia passes to the Union. After Rich Mountain (11 July 1861, bibliography entry) 'The Union army would occupy the western region of Virginia for the rest of the war'; the Restored Government of Virginia at Wheeling 'controlled only the areas held by federal forces'; statehood as West Virginia followed in 1863 (the page gives only the year).

region.text: the Choctaw and Chickasaw nations of the southern Indian Territory (approximate box)

ledger.note: 12 July 1861: treaty with the Choctaw and Chickasaw. 'On July 12, 1861, the Confederate government signed a treaty with both the Choctaw and Chickasaw Indian nations.' The page adds that the Indian Territory 'never formally joined the Confederacy, but did receive representation in the Congress'; the other nations' treaties are not on the page. Drawn as a client (lighter tint) at confidence 2; am-05 should write the nations.

region.text: the portion of the New Mexico Territory south of the 34th parallel

ledger.note: 1 August 1861: Confederate Arizona. 'On August 1, 1861, the victorious Baylor proclaimed the existence of a Confederate Arizona Territory', 'the portion of the New Mexico Territory south of the 34th parallel'; Mesilla and Tucson had voted to join on 16 March 1861 (CSA page) and Davis proclaimed the territory on 14 February 1862 (the two pages' dates for the organisation differ).

region.text: Kentucky: Confederate forces entered Columbus on 3 September 1861; Bowling Green was the Confederate capital of Kentucky

ledger.note: September 1861: Kentucky becomes a battleground. Grant seized Paducah on 5 September 1861, two days after Confederate forces entered Columbus (the page's dated lines, as read); the CSA page: 'Kentucky was admitted into the Confederacy on December 10, 1861', but the page also says the Confederate Kentucky government never controlled the state's people after 1862.

region.text: Missouri, whose secession ordinance was passed on 31 October 1861

ledger.note: October 1861: Missouri's secession ordinance. 'on October 31, 1861, it passed an ordinance of secession'; the Confederacy recognised the claimants on 28 November 1861. Page silent on the fighting before (Wilson's Creek and others are not on the pages opened), so the start is bridged from the ordinance.

region.text: western Virginia, where the Union column attacked at Philippi on 3 June 1861

ledger.note: December 1861: the Western Virginia campaign ends. The campaign table gives 'May to December, 1861'; the Union 'would occupy the western region of Virginia for the rest of the war', while the Kanawha Valley changed hands within the campaign (Cross Lanes, Kanawha Gap).

region.text: the difference between Cliopatria's 1861 and 1862 shapes, less the lands dated separately

ledger.note: 1862: residual losses between Cliopatria's 1861 and 1862 shapes that no page opened dates. By the gazetteer the 1862 shape keeps 55% of Arkansas (98% in 1861), 92% of North Carolina, 96% of Virginia, 87% of Louisiana, 95% of Mississippi and 97% of Florida; the Trans-Mississippi page has only Pea Ridge 'in northwest Arkansas in March 1862'. Page silent on where the lines ran; bridged from the shape difference.

region.text: Kentucky: Confederate forces entered Columbus on 3 September 1861; Bowling Green was the Confederate capital of Kentucky

ledger.note: February 1862: the Confederates leave Kentucky. After Fort Donelson (Buckner surrendered 'his command of 11,500 men' after fighting on 15 February) the page describes the Confederate withdrawal from Columbus; Bowling Green likewise. The exact day is not on the page.

region.text: Tennessee outside the east and the south-east that the 1862 shape keeps (Forts Henry and Donelson, February 1862)

ledger.note: February 1862: Forts Henry and Donelson open Tennessee. The Confederates withdrew from Fort Henry on 5 February; 'The Tennessee River was then open for future Union operations into the South'; Fort Donelson fell after fighting on 15 February. The page does not say that Nashville or Memphis fell; the lost land is the part of Tennessee missing from Cliopatria's 1862 shape.

region.text: Missouri, whose secession ordinance was passed on 31 October 1861

ledger.note: March 1862: Pea Ridge secures Missouri for the Union. The Union 'defeated the Confederate forces at the Battle of Pea Ridge in northwest Arkansas in March 1862' and held most of Missouri; Price's Raid of 1864 reopens the contest (below).

region.text: the northern half of the New Mexico Territory, north of the 34th parallel

ledger.note: 26-28 March 1862: Glorieta Pass. 'The Confederate loss at the Battle of Glorieta Pass forced Confederate retreat from the territory'; the CSA page: 'the Confederate New Mexico campaign to take the northern half of the U.S. territory failed' in 1862. The campaign's opening in the north is not dated on either page.

region.text: the northern half of the New Mexico Territory, north of the 34th parallel

ledger.note: April 1862: Picacho Pass ends the Confederate hold north of Mesilla. The Battle of Stanwix Station was 30 March 1862 and Picacho Pass 'the following month'; the California Column delayed but did not yet reach Mesilla.

region.text: New Orleans

ledger.note: 28 April 1862: New Orleans falls. 'Farragut captured New Orleans, the South's largest city and most significant seaport.' The CSA page has it 'captured on April 29' (infobox 'until May 1, 1862').

region.text: Corinth, Mississippi and its railroad junction

ledger.note: 29 May 1862: Corinth abandoned. Beauregard withdrew during the night of 29 May without a fight and Union forces occupied Corinth, in north Mississippi (the page's account, as read).

region.text: the portion of the New Mexico Territory south of the 34th parallel

ledger.note: 8 July 1862: Confederate Arizona falls. The infobox date of Union occupation is 8 July 1862; the Confederates abandoned Mesilla in July 1862 and retreated south to Franklin, Texas (page text, as read). 'For the rest of the war, California Column troops controlled all of Confederate Arizona.'

region.text: Tennessee east of the Chattanooga line that Cliopatria's 1863 shape no longer holds

ledger.note: 1863: East Tennessee and the Chattanooga line are lost. The Western Theater page dates Chickamauga (19-20 September) and the relief of Chattanooga (24-25 November) but not the occupation of East Tennessee (Knoxville): page silent. The land is Tennessee outside Cliopatria's 1863 shape, which keeps 17% of the state.

region.text: the difference between Cliopatria's 1862 and 1863 shapes, less the lands dated separately

ledger.note: 1863: residual losses between Cliopatria's 1862 and 1863 shapes beyond the lands dated above. By the gazetteer Alabama falls from 99% to 80%, Mississippi from 95% to 60%, Louisiana from 87% to 56% and Virginia from 96% to 87%. The Western Theater page dates only Vicksburg, Port Hudson and Chattanooga; page silent on the rest.

region.text: Vicksburg, Mississippi

ledger.note: 4 July 1863: Vicksburg surrenders. 'On July 4, Pemberton surrendered his army and the city to Grant.'

region.text: the Confederate shore of the Mississippi River from Island Number 10 to Vicksburg and Port Hudson

ledger.note: 8 July 1863: the Mississippi River is cut. 'By July 8, after Banks captured Port Hudson, the entire Mississippi River was in Union hands.' The CSA page: 'the Confederacy lost the Mississippi River following the capture of Vicksburg, Mississippi, and Port Hudson'; Texas, western Louisiana and Arkansas are cut off from the east.

region.text: Arkansas north and east of the south-west corner that Cliopatria's 1864 shape keeps

ledger.note: 10 September 1863: Little Rock falls and Arkansas shrinks to its south-west. The Little Rock campaign page: 'Little Rock's civilian government surrendered the city to the Union', 'With the fall of Little Rock, the Union controlled most of Arkansas', and 'Union forces garrisoned several other towns along the Arkansas River'. The land is Arkansas outside Cliopatria's 1864 shape (8% of the state against 53% in 1863), which is the January 1864 picture. Reviewer 2026-10-19: re-dated from 1864 (confidence 1, Trans-Mississippi page silent) to September 1863 on the Little Rock campaign page.

region.text: Chattanooga and the Tennessee-Georgia line

ledger.note: September 1863: the Chickamauga-Chattanooga campaign. Bragg attacked on 19-20 September and the Union forces retreated to Chattanooga (a Confederate victory, as the page is read).

region.text: Chattanooga and the Tennessee-Georgia line

ledger.note: 24-25 November 1863: Chattanooga relieved. Union attacks lifted the siege; 'Chattanooga was saved.'

region.text: Missouri, whose secession ordinance was passed on 31 October 1861

ledger.note: 1864: Price's Raid. The page gives the end, not the start: the raid 'ended when Price's troops were defeated in the Battle of Westport that October'. A Confederate attempt to retake Missouri.

region.text: the difference between Cliopatria's 1863 and 1864 shapes, less the lands dated separately

ledger.note: 1864: residual loss between Cliopatria's 1863 and 1864 shapes: Georgia falls from 100% to 95% by the gazetteer, the rest being the Arkansas loss above. The Western Theater page dates Chickamauga (19-20 September) and Chattanooga (24-25 November 1863); page silent on the exact lines.

region.text: Atlanta

ledger.note: 1 September 1864: Atlanta falls. Hood evacuated Atlanta on the night of 1 September (the page does not give 2 September).

region.text: Georgia outside the south-west corner the 1865 shape keeps: Atlanta, the March to the Sea and Savannah

ledger.note: September-November 1864: the March to the Sea. 'Sherman's March to the Sea to take Savannah' followed the fall of Atlanta (the start of the march is not dated on the page).

region.text: Missouri, whose secession ordinance was passed on 31 October 1861

ledger.note: October 1864: Westport. 'Price's Raid ended when Price's troops were defeated in the Battle of Westport that October'; Missouri stays Union.

region.text: Georgia outside the south-west corner the 1865 shape keeps: Atlanta, the March to the Sea and Savannah

ledger.note: 22 December 1864: Savannah. 'Sherman entered on December 22, 1864.' The swath of Georgia between Atlanta and the coast goes with it; Cliopatria's 1865 shape keeps 43% of Georgia.

region.text: Georgia outside the south-west corner the 1865 shape keeps: Atlanta, the March to the Sea and Savannah

ledger.note: 22 December 1864: the March to the Sea ends at Savannah ('Sherman entered on December 22, 1864').

region.text: the difference between Cliopatria's 1864 and 1865 shapes, less the lands dated separately

ledger.note: 1865: residual losses between Cliopatria's 1864 and 1865 shapes beyond Georgia (Savannah, above). By the gazetteer Alabama falls from 80% to 52%, Mississippi from 60% to 24% and South Carolina from 100% to 97%. The Western Theater page mentions Farragut's Mobile Bay victory without a date and says Mobile 'remained in Confederate hands'; page silent on Alabama and Mississippi.

region.text: the Carolinas, Columbia (17 February 1865) to Johnston's surrender (26 April 1865)

ledger.note: 17 February 1865: the Carolinas campaign takes Columbia. 'On February 17, Columbia surrendered to Sherman.'

region.text: Columbia, South Carolina

ledger.note: 17 February 1865: Columbia, South Carolina. 'On February 17, Columbia surrendered to Sherman.'

region.text: Wilmington, North Carolina

ledger.note: 22 February 1865: Wilmington. 'The last significant Confederate seaport, Wilmington, surrendered on February 22.'
3 April 1865: the government leaves Richmond for Danville. Infobox: 'Richmond, Virginia (until April 2-3, 1865)'; 'Danville, Virginia (until April 10, 1865)'.

region.text: Virginia: Richmond and Petersburg (2-3 April), Lee at Appomattox (9 April 1865)

ledger.note: 2-3 April 1865: Richmond falls. 'When the Union broke through Lee's lines at Petersburg, Richmond fell immediately.' 'Lee surrendered at Appomattox Court House, Virginia, on April 9, 1865.' Virginia is the land.
10 April 1865: the government moves from Danville to Greensboro, North Carolina (infobox: 'Danville, Virginia (until April 10, 1865)'; 'Greensboro, North Carolina (until May 5, 1865)').

region.text: the Carolinas, Columbia (17 February 1865) to Johnston's surrender (26 April 1865)

ledger.note: 26 April 1865: Johnston surrenders. He 'formally surrendered his army and all Confederate forces in the Carolinas, Georgia, and Florida.'

region.text: the Carolinas, Georgia and Florida

ledger.note: 26 April 1865: the Carolinas, Georgia and Florida surrender. 'Johnston formally surrendered his army and all Confederate forces in the Carolinas, Georgia, and Florida.' The CSA infobox gives 'Military collapse: April 26, 1865'.

region.text: the Choctaw and Chickasaw nations of the southern Indian Territory (approximate box)

ledger.note: 1865: the Confederate relation with the Indian Territory ends with the Confederacy. The page gives no date for the nations' surrender; the Trans-Mississippi page puts the Union's Honey Springs victory on 17 July 1863 'to secure Indian Territory' without saying that the Union fully held it. Year bridged from the Confederacy's end.

region.text: the Trans-Mississippi Department: Texas and what is left of Louisiana and Arkansas

ledger.note: 26 May 1865: the Trans-Mississippi Department surrenders. The Confederate Arizona infobox gives 26 May 1865 'as the surrender of the Trans-Mississippi Department at Shreveport, Louisiana'; the Trans-Mississippi page has Kirby Smith surrendering at Galveston (no date); the last battle, Palmito Ranch in south Texas (12-13 May), was a Confederate victory.

region.text: the last Confederate land in 1865

ledger.note: 5 May 1865: the Confederate States of America ends. Infobox: 'Military collapse: April 26, 1865' and 'Debellation and dissolution: May 5, 1865'; the Confederate Congress had ceased 'as a legislative body on March 18'; 'President Davis was captured May 10.' Confederate forces in Alabama and Mississippi and the Trans-Mississippi (26 May) surrendered after the infobox date; the page is silent on those two.

wars.name: Western Theater of the American Civil War

zones.text: Kentucky: Confederate forces entered Columbus on 3 September 1861; Bowling Green was the Confederate capital of Kentucky
Tennessee outside the east and the south-east that the 1862 shape keeps (Forts Henry and Donelson, February 1862)
the Confederate shore of the Mississippi River from Island Number 10 to Vicksburg and Port Hudson
Georgia outside the south-west corner the 1865 shape keeps: Atlanta, the March to the Sea and Savannah
the Carolinas, Columbia (17 February 1865) to Johnston's surrender (26 April 1865)

wars.outcome: Union victory: Kentucky and Tennessee lost in 1862, New Orleans 28 April, Corinth 29 May 1862, Vicksburg and Port Hudson in July 1863, Atlanta 1 September and Savannah 22 December 1864, Columbia and Wilmington in February 1865, Johnston's surrender 26 April 1865.
wars.note: Nashville, Memphis, Knoxville and Mobile are not on the page; the ledger marks those years at confidence 1 where Cliopatria's shape has to be explained.

wars.name: Trans-Mississippi Theater of the American Civil War

zones.text: Missouri, whose secession ordinance was passed on 31 October 1861
the Choctaw and Chickasaw nations of the southern Indian Territory (approximate box)

wars.outcome: Missouri held by the Union after Pea Ridge (March 1862); Honey Springs (17 July 1863) 'to secure Indian Territory'; the Red River campaign (1864) thwarted and the Union invasions of Texas 'each of them unsuccessful'; Kirby Smith surrendered his command in 1865.
wars.note: The page does not mention Little Rock or Fort Smith.

wars.name: Western Virginia campaign

zones.text: western Virginia, where the Union column attacked at Philippi on 3 June 1861

wars.outcome: Union victory: Philippi (3 June) and Rich Mountain (11 July) 1861; the Union 'would occupy the western region of Virginia for the rest of the war' and the Restored Government of Virginia (Wheeling) led to West Virginia.
wars.note: The Kanawha Valley changed hands within the campaign (Cross Lanes, Kanawha Gap); small Confederate brigades held the south and east for much of the war.

wars.name: New Mexico campaign

zones.text: the northern half of the New Mexico Territory, north of the 34th parallel
the portion of the New Mexico Territory south of the 34th parallel

wars.outcome: Confederate defeat: Glorieta Pass 26-28 March 1862, Stanwix Station 30 March, Picacho Pass April; the Confederates abandon Mesilla in July 1862 and the California Column holds Confederate Arizona to the end.
wars.note: The Confederate Arizona page gives the Territory proclaimed on 1 August 1861; the campaign itself is named on the CSA page ('the Confederate New Mexico campaign to take the northern half of the U.S. territory failed').

wars.name: Red River campaign
wars.outcome: Union failure: the Union 'tried to gain control over northwestern Louisiana, but was thwarted'.

wars.name: Price's Raid

zones.text: Missouri, whose secession ordinance was passed on 31 October 1861

wars.outcome: Confederate failure: the raid 'ended when Price's troops were defeated in the Battle of Westport that October'; Missouri stays Union.
wars.note: The start of the raid is not dated on the page.

wars.name: Sherman's March to the Sea

zones.text: Georgia outside the south-west corner the 1865 shape keeps: Atlanta, the March to the Sea and Savannah

wars.outcome: Union victory: Atlanta evacuated 1 September 1864, Savannah entered 22 December 1864.
wars.note: Mobile Bay (August 1864) is mentioned without a date and Mobile 'remained in Confederate hands'.

wars.name: Carolinas campaign

zones.text: the Carolinas, Columbia (17 February 1865) to Johnston's surrender (26 April 1865)

wars.outcome: Union victory: Columbia 17 February, Wilmington 22 February, Johnston's surrender of the Carolinas, Georgia and Florida on 26 April 1865.

wars.name: Appomattox campaign
wars.outcome: Union victory: Lee's lines broken at Petersburg, Richmond fell 2-3 April, Lee surrendered at Appomattox Court House on 9 April 1865.
wars.note: Opened only through the CSA page; the Eastern Theater and Appomattox pages are outside the page budget.

certainty.note: The frontier with the Union follows the pre-war state lines (and Virginia's line); the exceptions are the contested border states (Kentucky, Missouri, western Virginia), Confederate Arizona and the Indian Territory, which are soft.

The front lines move by campaign and are approximate; the Cliopatria shapes are snapshots, and the 1862-65 shapes are dated by the ledger's captures. The Texas, Louisiana and Gulf coast edges remain state lines.

notes:
Rebel state: type 'rebel' (the Confederacy held land for four years). The Cliopatria shapes (1861 1.71 M, 1862 1.49 M, 1863 1.32 M, 1864 1.25 M, 1865 1.08 M km2) are year snapshots of the Confederate states; all five are adjusted for Texas (only the Republic of Texas outline, 55% of the state, is inside) and 1861 also for West Virginia (98% inside) and Confederate Arizona; the infobox of the CSA page gives no area, so the area check was impossible and the population shares on the page (72% at the end of April 1862, 53% early 1864, one third early 1865) are the only sanity test: they sit below the area shares (87%, 73%, 63% of the 1861 area), as they should for lost populous valleys.

Page budget used up (5 of 5): Confederate States of America, Confederate Arizona, Western Theater, Trans-Mississippi Theater, Western Virginia campaign. Not covered and recorded at confidence 1 or left to a gap-filler: Nashville and Memphis (1862), Knoxville and East Tennessee (1863), Little Rock and the Arkansas valley (1863-64), the Gulf coast (Mobile, Pensacola, Roanoke Island and New Bern in 1862), Alabama and Mississippi in 1865 (Selma, Mobile, Taylor's surrender), Palmito Ranch beyond one line, the Union occupation of Brownsville and Galveston. A gap-filler should open Eastern Theater, Anaconda Plan, Knoxville campaign, Little Rock campaign and Conclusion of the American Civil War.

Disagreements between pages: New Orleans captured 28 April (Western Theater) or 29 April (CSA page); the Confederate Arizona organisation 18 January 1862 (infobox) or Davis's proclamation 14 February 1862 (text); Texas admission 2 March 1861 in the USA dossier (Territory page) against 'February 1; referendum February 23' on the CSA page; Tennessee 'May 7; referendum June 8' (the ledger uses June).

States that need dossiers elsewhere: the Choctaw Nation and Chickasaw Nation (Indian Territory allies, group am-05) and the Restored Government of Virginia / West Virginia (the USA dossier's province, group am-07). Kentucky and Missouri's Confederate governments (admitted 10 December and 28 November 1861) are drawn only as contested zones, not as territory, because the Confederacy never held them; their 'shadow' governments were in Bowling Green and Marshall, Texas (page).

Gazetteer: the specs use real Natural Earth names; 'Corinth, Mississippi' has no place entry and is a radius around its coordinates (list under gazetteer_names_needed); the Choctaw-Chickasaw lands and the 34th-parallel splits are polygon boxes, approximate.
